# google_dataflow_config_store_setting

A regional Dataflow Config Store setting on a project, folder, or organization.


To get more information about ConfigStoreSetting, see:

* [API documentation](https://cloud.google.com/dataflow/docs/reference/rest/v1b3/projects.locations.configStoreSettings)
* How-to Guides
    * [Dataflow Config Store Settings](https://cloud.google.com/dataflow/docs/guides/config-store-settings)

## Example Usage - Dataflow Config Store Setting Basic


```hcl
data "google_project" "project" {
}

resource "google_dataflow_config_store_setting" "example" {
  parent                  = "projects/${data.google_project.project.number}"
  location                = "us-central1"
  config_store_setting_id = "default_launcher_machine_type"
  value {
    string_value = "e2-standard-4"
  }
}
```

## Argument Reference

The following arguments are supported:


* `value` -
  (Required)
  The configuration value of the setting.
  Structure is [documented below](#nested_value).

* `parent` -
  (Required)
  The parent resource in which to create the config store setting.
  Must be in one of the following formats:
  * `projects/{project_number}` (numeric project number is required)
  * `folders/{folder_id}`
  * `organizations/{organization_id}`

* `location` -
  (Required)
  The Dataflow region for the setting (e.g. `us-central1`).

* `config_store_setting_id` -
  (Required)
  The ID of the config store setting (e.g. `default_launcher_machine_type`).


* `deletion_policy` - (Optional) Whether Terraform will be prevented from destroying the resource. Defaults to DELETE.
	When a 'terraform destroy' or 'terraform apply' would delete the resource,
	the command will fail if this field is set to "PREVENT" in Terraform state.
	When set to "ABANDON", the command will remove the resource from Terraform
	management without updating or deleting the resource in the API.
	When set to "DELETE", deleting the resource is allowed.


<a name="nested_value"></a>The `value` block supports:

* `string_value` -
  (Optional)
  Represents a string value.

* `bool_value` -
  (Optional)
  Represents a boolean value.

## Attributes Reference

In addition to the arguments listed above, the following computed attributes are exported:

* `id` - an identifier for the resource with format `{{parent}}/locations/{{location}}/configStoreSettings/{{config_store_setting_id}}`

* `name` -
  The resource name of the setting.
  Format: `projects/{project_number}/locations/{location}/configStoreSettings/{config_store_setting_id}`
  or `folders/{folder_id}/locations/{location}/configStoreSettings/{config_store_setting_id}`
  or `organizations/{organization_id}/locations/{location}/configStoreSettings/{config_store_setting_id}`


## Timeouts

This resource provides the following
[Timeouts](https://developer.hashicorp.com/terraform/plugin/sdkv2/resources/retries-and-customizable-timeouts) configuration options:

- `create` - Default is 20 minutes.
- `update` - Default is 20 minutes.
- `delete` - Default is 20 minutes.

## Import


ConfigStoreSetting can be imported using any of these accepted formats:

* `{{parent}}/locations/{{location}}/configStoreSettings/{{config_store_setting_id}}`

In Terraform v1.12.0 and later, use an [`identity` block](https://developer.hashicorp.com/terraform/language/block/import#identity) to import ConfigStoreSetting using identity values. For example:

```tf
import {
  identity = {
    parent = "<-required value->"
    location = "<-required value->"
    configStoreSettingId = "<-required value->"
  }
  to = google_dataflow_config_store_setting.default
}
```

In Terraform v1.5.0 and later, use an [`import` block](https://developer.hashicorp.com/terraform/language/import) to import ConfigStoreSetting using one of the formats above. For example:

```tf
import {
  id = "{{parent}}/locations/{{location}}/configStoreSettings/{{config_store_setting_id}}"
  to = google_dataflow_config_store_setting.default
}
```

When using the [`terraform import` command](https://developer.hashicorp.com/terraform/cli/commands/import), ConfigStoreSetting can be imported using one of the formats above. For example:

```
$ terraform import google_dataflow_config_store_setting.default {{parent}}/locations/{{location}}/configStoreSettings/{{config_store_setting_id}}
```
